courses.name: Woodbine Bend Golf Course
courses.about: Woodbine Bend Golf Course (Stockton, Illinois) is played from the gold tees. Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, ponds, buildings and the out-of-bounds line from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); fairways traced from USDA NAIP aerial imagery; trees from USGS 3DEP lidar; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: Bob Lohmann’s links-style layout (2002) rolls through driftless hills with mounds, tall native grass, a creek and ponds to keep us honest. Nineteen rounds in, Nick's nose becomes a faucet every year, Joe broke a club once, Kevin had diarrhea multiple times in the outhouse by #14, Craig always gets mad, and Andy aced #7 in 2026 and has told everyone. Our Galena!!! golfing home away from home.

courses.name: The South Course at Eagle Ridge
courses.about: The South Course at Eagle Ridge Resort & Spa (Galena, Illinois; Roger Packard, 1984) is played from the gold tees. Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, fairways, ponds, streams and the out-of-bounds line from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); trees from USGS 3DEP lidar; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: Roger Packard’s 1984 design at Eagle Ridge Resort plays through dense woods and a dramatic, hidden valley, with narrow fairways, big elevation changes and a par 72 of about 6,350 yards from the gold tees. Slope 136 and a 71.8 rating make it one of the hardest cards we play. This is where the trip began in 2007: four dudes, Kalle’s mom’s condo, and scores that peaked at 110.

courses.name: The North Course at Eagle Ridge
courses.about: The North Course at Eagle Ridge Resort & Spa (Galena, Illinois; Roger Packard, 1977) is played from the gold tees. Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, fairways, ponds, streams and the out-of-bounds line from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); trees from USGS 3DEP lidar; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: Roger Packard’s 1977 woodland layout was the first course at Eagle Ridge Resort: a par 72 of about 6,400 yards from the gold tees (71.4/131) with big greens that break more than they look, and an 8th tee towering high above the green that needs a shot clipping the corner of Lake Galena. Three visits, three excuses: Brian’s 9:00 a.m. departure policy, Craig and Kevin flaming out early, and a skunk in a creepy house closet keeping everyone awake.

courses.card:
Legends Course
at Memphis National GC
courses.about: The Legends Course at Memphis National Golf Club (Collierville, Tennessee; Ed Seay and Arnold Palmer, 1971; par 72) is played from the white tees (6,274 yd); black, gold and green are the markers. Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, ponds and cart paths from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); fairways traced from the 2023 USDA NAIP aerial; trees from the 2012 Shelby County lidar (USGS), checked against the aerial; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: An Arnold Palmer and Ed Seay design from 1971 at Memphis National, about 12 miles east of Memphis: a par 72 of about 6,300 yards from the white tees (70.5/126) with a creek running through it and houses lining the edges. One of Kalle's southern home courses. The crew hasn’t played it yet. Barbecue, Palmer pedigree and 1971 charm we’re old enough to appreciate; somebody add it to the rotation?

courses.name: The General at Eagle Ridge
courses.about: The General Course at Eagle Ridge Resort & Spa (Galena, Illinois; Andy North and Roger Packard, 1997) is played from the 3-Star tees (6,245 yards). Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, fairways, ponds, streams and the out-of-bounds line from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); trees from USGS 3DEP lidar; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: Roger Packard and Andy North’s 1997 layout at Eagle Ridge, named for Galena’s Ulysses S. Grant, winds through old quarries and forest and is the toughest test on that property: slope 137 from the tips, and a par 72 of about 6,250 yards (70.6/132) from the 3-Star tees we play. We played it once, in 2011, on a huge discount after landslide inducing rains; the trip log reads “Hot tubbbbbbb" to commemorate the year. Priorities.

courses.name: Fossil Trace Golf Club
courses.about: Fossil Trace Golf Club (Golden, Colorado; Jim Engh, 2003) is played from the blue tees (6,241 yards). Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, fairways, ponds, streams and the out-of-bounds line from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); trees from USGS 3DEP lidar; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: Jim Engh’s 2003 design on a former clay mine at the foot of the Rockies, in Golden, with real dinosaur tracks in the sandstone on 12, big-contoured greens and a par 72 of about 6,250 yards from the blue tees (68.9/130). At nearly 5,800 feet, thin air adds about 8% to every carry in the game, our best shot at a long-drive trophy. Nate and Kalle played this with Andy while visiting him in Arvada, CO. It was glorious and followed up with various pickled things at local restaurants.

courses.name: Stonehenge Golf Club
courses.about: Stonehenge Golf Club (Barrington, Illinois) is played from the blue tees. Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, fairways, ponds, streams and the out-of-bounds line from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); trees from the 2007 Lake County lidar (USGS); the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: A 1972 Charles Maddox design along IL 22 in Barrington, par 72 and nearly 6,850 yards from the tips (6,350 from the blue tees we play, 70.5/130). Close enough to Chicago for a Portillo’s or Lou Malnati’s Champions Dinner, which is honestly the whole pitch. This was Kalle's northern home course, and has been played by all the pals at various times. Nate got hit in the head by a shank on #2 once, sorry, Nate.

courses.name: Thunderhawk Golf Club
courses.about: Thunderhawk Golf Club (Beach Park, Illinois; Robert Trent Jones Jr., 1999; Lake County Forest Preserves) is played from the bronze tees. Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, fairways, ponds and the out-of-bounds line from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); trees from the 2007 Lake County lidar (USGS), checked against the 2023 USDA NAIP aerial; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: A Robert Trent Jones Jr. design (1999), the Lake County Forest Preserves’ flagship on 243 acres of old farmland with oak and hickory groves and more than 7,000 yards from the tips (about 6,350 from the bronze tees we play, slope 134). Called “the benchmark” of Chicago public golf. Close to Wisconsin, so the cheese is always to blame. Andy, Kalle, Brian, Kevin, and Craig have all played it. Including one infamous round for Andy's birthday where it was 45 degrees and rainy with a strong wind.

courses.name: Bear Slide Golf Club
courses.about: Bear Slide Golf Club (Cicero, Indiana; Hamilton County) is played from the white tees (par 71, 5,966 yd); black, blue and red are the markers. Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, ponds and the out-of-bounds line from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); fairways traced from the 2022 USDA NAIP aerial where OpenStreetMap has none; trees from the 2017 Hamilton County lidar (USGS), checked against the aerial; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: Dean Refram’s design north of Indianapolis has a Scottish links-style front nine, a traditional back nine and a creek wandering through it, a par 71 of nearly 7,000 yards from the tips (about 5,950 from the white tees we play, 69.4/122), ranked the 14th best course in America by Golf Advisor in 2018. We played it on our one trip to Indiana (2024), and experienced a house bathroom with a car stereo and a day off for our knees.

courses.name: Galena Golf Club
courses.about: Galena Golf Club (Galena, Illinois; par 72) is played from the white tees (6,368 yd); blue, gold and red are the markers. Alpha: built from OpenStreetMap alone. Hole lines, greens, bunkers, fairways, the pond and streams from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); three tee boxes OSM lacks placed off the aerial; trees from the 2019 Jo Daviess lidar (USGS), checked against the 2023 USDA NAIP aerial; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: Just off US 20 outside Galena, a hilly, tree-lined layout that began as nine holes long ago and got its second nine in 1994: a par 72 of about 6,400 yards from the white tees (71.4/122), with plenty of long par 4s and passing trucks for spectators. Five rounds have been played here. Those years included a wiffle ball in the road, a keg of Coors Light, and 2021, when Woodbine had a tournament and we landed here.

courses.name: Maxwelton Braes Golf Resort
courses.about: Maxwelton Braes Golf Resort (Baileys Harbor, Wisconsin; par 72, 1929) is played from the green tees (6,041 yd); gold, white, blue and orange are the markers. Beta: built from OpenStreetMap, the 2018 Wisconsin lidar and the 2022 NAIP aerial, with the scorecard from 18Birdies.
courses.blurb: Door County’s historic 1929 layout by Roseman and O’Neil, tucked beside the Maxwelton Braes Lodge in Baileys Harbor, with Highway 57 cutting through the middle and dense woods on nearly every side. A par 72 of about 6,000 yards from the green tees (69.5/119), short enough to be friendly. It’s Andy’s home course, so he knows every bounce and isn’t telling.

courses.name: Elbel Park Golf Course
courses.about: Elbel Park Golf Course (South Bend, Indiana) is played from the Sand Hill tees (6,441 yd); Cardinal, Heron and Egret are the markers. Alpha: built from OpenStreetMap alone. Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, fairways and water from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); trees from the 2017 Indiana statewide lidar (USGS), checked against the 2023 USDA NAIP aerial; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: A city-run 1963 Toth & Toth design built around Mud Lake in South Bend, with water in play on 13 holes and nearly 6,900 yards of par 72 from the back tees (about 6,450 from the Sand Hill tees we play, 70.5/121). Our 2022 visit came with a garage hot tub, a bags tournament and a Friday-night head start, and Nick walked away with the Brown Jacket.

North Course

Alpha: built from OpenStreetMap alone. Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, fairways and water from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); trees from the 2017 Hamilton County lidar (USGS), checked against the 2023 USDA NAIP aerial; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: A Kern-family design (Ron and Gary Kern) in Noblesville with links-style touches, a par 70 of about 6,450 yards from the tips (5,975 from the white tees we play, 69.7/122) and a recent bunker remodel to dodge. We squeezed it in on a Saturday in 2024 after a Friday pontoon-boat day off, and Joe took the jacket.

courses.name: Lacoma Golf Course (Blue)
courses.about: The Blue course at Lacoma Golf Club (East Dubuque, Illinois; par 71) is played from the white tees (6,295 yd); blue, gold and red are the markers. Alpha: built from OpenStreetMap alone. Hole lines, greens, tees, bunkers, fairways and water from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); trees from the 2019 Jo Daviess lidar (USGS), checked against the 2023 USDA NAIP aerial; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: Gordon Cunningham’s rolling layout in the wooded hills of the Mississippi valley above East Dubuque, the toughest of the club’s three regulation courses, with sand on nearly every hole and a par 71 of about 6,300 yards from the white tees (70.7/120). Two visits, 2010 (the Dwarf house) and 2021 (Pandemic Galena!!! part 2), and Nick and Craig each took the jacket.

courses.name: Briar Leaf Golf Club
courses.about: Briar Leaf Golf Club (La Porte, Indiana; par 72, closed in 2026) is played from the silver tees (6,217 yd); black, gold and green are the markers. Alpha: built from OpenStreetMap alone, and OpenStreetMap has no hole lines or tee boxes there, so the order of the holes and the tee boxes are a best guess from the scorecard lengths. Greens, bunkers, some fairways, water and cart paths from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL); trees from the 2017 Indiana statewide lidar (USGS), checked against the 2022 USDA NAIP aerial; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model.
courses.blurb: A 1973 layout in La Porte, Indiana, with water on eight holes, an island green, rolling hills, plenty of sand and a par 72 of about 6,600 yards from the tips (6,217 from the silver tees, 70.4/128). We played it in 2022 on the Buffalena!!! weekend, where the food was plentiful and Nick took the jacket. The course closed in 2026 for housing, so the game is now the way back.

courses.name: Chestnut Mountain Disc Golf
courses.about: Disc golf (alpha) on the ski hill at Chestnut Mountain Resort (Galena, Illinois; 9 holes, 2010): the nine played twice, from the long tees and then the short ones. Throw with the tempo bar as for a golf swing; the strike dot sets the release angle (hyzer or anhyzer) and the nose. Rounds here are not posted to the world leaderboard. Hole lengths from UDisc; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model, trees from USGS 3DEP lidar, buildings, ponds and roads from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
courses.blurb: Chestnut Mountain’s disc course: nine baskets with two tees each, up and down a wooded bluff above the Mississippi, played twice to make eighteen. We tried it once in 2026 with mini golf for dessert. The scenery gets 4.8 stars; our form, fewer.

courses.name: Adler Park Disc Golf
courses.about: Disc golf (alpha) in Adler Memorial Park (Libertyville, Illinois; 9 holes, 1981): a town park course through wooded ravines and open lawns above the Des Plaines River, with one tee per hole, so the nine is played twice. Throw with the tempo bar as for a golf swing; the strike dot sets the release angle (hyzer or anhyzer) and the nose. Rounds here are not posted to the world leaderboard. Tees and baskets from the course sign's map, hole lengths from its card; the ground from the USGS 3DEP 1 m elevation model, trees from the 2007 Lake County lidar (USGS), buildings, the river and roads from © OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL).
courses.blurb: Adler Park, Libertyville: nine baskets through hilly woods along the Des Plaines River, which only bites on 9 if you really overcook it. Free to play, about an hour a round, and we play it twice for eighteen. Not played yet, but we’re stretching.
